text:
Complete application lifecycle

Diagram
flowchart TD
    A[Business idea and desired outcomes] --> B[Discovery: users, problems, value, constraints, success measures]
    B --> C{Idea viable?}
    C -->|No| A
    C -->|Yes| D[Requirements: journeys, rules, data, integrations, security, acceptance criteria]
    D --> E[Solution design: architecture, UX, data model, interfaces, controls, operations]
    E --> F[Planning: scope, increments, estimates, ownership, dependencies, risks]
    F --> G[Development: code, configuration, migrations, documentation, reviews]
    G --> H[Continuous integration: build, static analysis, automated checks]
    H --> I[Testing: functional, integration, security, accessibility, performance, acceptance]
    I --> J{Quality criteria met?}
    J -->|No| G
    J -->|Yes| K[Release: version, approvals, notes, training, support and rollback readiness]
    K --> L[Deployment: provision, configure, migrate, promote and verify]
    L --> M{Production healthy?}
    M -->|No| N[Rollback or remediate]
    N --> G
    M -->|Yes| O[Operations: monitor, support, secure, back up, maintain and respond]
    O --> P[Continuous improvement: analyze telemetry, incidents, feedback and outcomes]
    P --> B
    Q[Connected knowledge record: decisions, requirements, designs, work, tests, versions and telemetry]
    B -. updates .-> Q
    D -. updates .-> Q
    E -. updates .-> Q
    F -. updates .-> Q
    G -. updates .-> Q
    I -. updates .-> Q
    K -. updates .-> Q
    L -. updates .-> Q
    O -. updates .-> Q
    P -. updates .-> Q

Because the platform is unidentified, this is a representative lifecycle rather than a claim about specific product capabilities.
limitations: The platform’s identity and confirmed lifecycle features were not supplied.
